grammar.title: Talking about actions that will (or would) have finished
grammar.intro: Two compound tenses let you look at completed actions from a distance. The future perfect (habré + participle) says what will have happened by a certain point — or guesses about the recent past. The conditional perfect (habría + participle) says what would have happened in another version of events. Both just need the right form of haber plus a past participle.

sections.heading: Future perfect: habré + participle
sections.body: Use it for something that will already be finished by a future moment. Conjugate haber in the future and add the participle:

ex.en: By tomorrow I will have finished the report.
By then we will have already arrived.

sections.heading: Guessing about the recent past
sections.body: The future perfect also expresses a guess about something that just happened — English uses "must have":

ex.en: He must have already left; he isn't answering.
ex.note: habrá salido = he must have left

ex.es: ¿Dónde está? Se habrá olvidado de la cita.
ex.en: Where is he? He must have forgotten the appointment.

sections.heading: Conditional perfect: habría + participle
sections.body: Use it for what would have happened — often a regret or a hypothetical about the past. Conjugate haber in the conditional and add the participle:

ex.en: If I were you, I would have studied more.
It would have been better to wait.

takeaways: Future perfect = habré/habrás/habrá… + participle: 'will have done'.
It also guesses about the recent past: Habrá salido = He must have left.
Conditional perfect = habría/habrías/habría… + participle: 'would have done'.
Common participles: hecho, visto, dicho, ido, sido.
Handy time markers: para mañana, para entonces.

mistakes.w: Para mañana habría terminado el informe.
mistakes.r: Para mañana habré terminado el informe.
mistakes.why: A real future deadline needs the future auxiliary (habré), not the conditional (habría).

mistakes.w: Yo que tú, habría estudiar más.
mistakes.r: Yo que tú, habría estudiado más.
mistakes.why: After haber you need the participle (estudiado), not the infinitive.

mistakes.w: Habrá salido ya; no ha contestado, así que ha ido seguro.
mistakes.why: The future perfect already carries the 'must have' guess — don't add 'seguro' as if it were certain.

exercises.prompt_en: By tomorrow I will have finished the report.
exercises.ok: ¡Correcto! Un plazo futuro → futuro perfecto: habré terminado.
exercises.no: A future deadline uses the future perfect: “habré terminado”.

exercises.prompt_en: He isn't answering the phone. He must have left already.
exercises.ok: ¡Exacto! El futuro perfecto expresa una suposición: habrá salido.
exercises.no: A guess about the recent past uses the future perfect: “Habrá salido”.

exercises.prompt: Build: “I would have gone to the party.”
exercises.no: “Yo habría ido a la fiesta” — conditional perfect: habría + participle.

exercises.prompt: Habría ___ mejor esperar un poco. (to be)
exercises.prompt_en: It would have been better to wait a little.
exercises.no: The participle of ser is “sido”: habría sido mejor.

exercises.prompt: Match each form to its meaning.

exercises.tts: Para el lunes habré leído el libro.
accepted: para el lunes habre leido el libro
exercises.translation: By Monday I will have read the book.
exercises.ok: ¡Correcto! “Para el lunes habré leído el libro.”
exercises.no: It was: “Para el lunes habré leído el libro.” (By Monday I will have read the book.)

exercises.scenario: A friend regrets missing an exam 📚

lines.speaker: Marcos
lines.es: Suspendí el examen. No estudié nada.
lines.en: I failed the exam. I didn't study at all.

options.text: Yo que tú, habría estudiado la noche antes.
Yo que tú, habré estudiado la noche antes.
Yo que tú, habría estudiar la noche antes.

exercises.ok: ¡Perfecto! Consejo sobre el pasado → condicional perfecto: habría estudiado.
exercises.no: Advice about the past uses the conditional perfect: “habría estudiado”.

exercises.en: By then I will have already finished.
exercises.no: Almost — tap “Hear it”, then match the sound.

vocab.en: he must have left / will have left
